content.title: About
content.content: A cookie, peanut butter sandwich consists of two soft cookie layers glued together with a creamy peanut butter filling. It is a popular quick snack, suitable for children’s lunches and often included in school meal programs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial peanut butter sandwich cookie appeared in the United States in the 1970s.
Peanut butter used in the sandwich is often fortified with vitamin E and plant sterols.
Cookies can be either soft or crunchy depending on the manufacturer’s recipe.
In some markets the product is sold as two separate cookies with a separate sachet of filling.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Peanut butter is rich in monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Peanut butter provides about 25 % protein, making the sandwich a good plant‑based protein source.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The filling contains niacin, thiamine and folate, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Peanuts supply magnesium, phosphorus and iron, which aid normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The sandwich quickly replenishes energy stores, convenient for active people and children.

items.title: Peanut allergy
items.content: Peanuts are a strong allergen; individuals with a peanut allergy should avoid this product.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The sandwich is relatively high in calories and fats, so portion control is recommended.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Cookies often contain added sugar; people monitoring blood glucose should take this into account.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some versions contain added salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is ready to eat straight from the package. It can be cut into smaller pieces for kids, added to lunchboxes, or used as a quick post‑workout snack.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place with the package tightly sealed. For longer storage (over 3 months) keep refrigerated to prevent the peanut butter from going rancid.
